description: We are the AgriOrbit team . we have an interest in technology, agriculture, and space science, and so, we have chosen the Field shift, adapting farms with NASA data challenge. we aim to explore NASA data and turn it into a practical solution that helps farmers adapt to the changing of environmental conditions. our team will use problem solving, coding, data analysis, and communication skills to solve this challenge.
summary:
We developed a solution that solves the problems: blind crop selection, expensive and slow lab tests, and climate unpredictability.
First, we researched and gathered the materials needed for our solution. Second, we made the codes and programmed the Arduino to send data needed for the farmer and display it on the web app.
The prototype consists of a moisture and humidity sensor, pH sensor, MPK sensor, a temperature sensor, and an ESP 32D Arduino.
The data collected by the Arduino combined with the NASA data about the climate and the weather those days will be used to inform the farmer about the best crop rotation plan for 2 seasons.
details:
AgriOrbit: Smart Crop Rotation Planning System

AgriOrbit is a smart crop rotation planning system designed to help farmers make more informed agricultural decisions while maintaining soil fertility, improving water-use efficiency, and promoting sustainable farming practices. The system aims to address one of the major challenges in agriculture: the continuous cultivation of crops without properly considering their impact on soil nutrients and the availability of natural resources.

The main idea behind AgriOrbit is to combine real-time soil measurements, NASA Earth observation data, and farmers' preferences to generate practical crop rotation recommendations for two consecutive growing seasons. Instead of relying entirely on traditional farming practices or general agricultural recommendations, the system provides decisions based on the specific environmental and soil conditions of each agricultural area.

How the System Works

AgriOrbit begins by collecting information about the selected agricultural field through soil sensors. These sensors measure important soil properties, particularly pH levels and the three primary plant nutrients: Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K). These nutrients play essential roles in plant growth and development. Nitrogen supports leaf and stem growth, phosphorus contributes to root development and energy transfer, and potassium helps regulate several physiological processes, including water balance and disease resistance.

By measuring these parameters, the system can identify potential nutrient deficiencies or unsuitable soil conditions that may affect crop growth. The collected measurements are then processed and used to establish an initial understanding of the soil's condition.

In addition to ground-based measurements, AgriOrbit integrates NASA Earth observation data to examine the environmental conditions surrounding the agricultural field. Relevant datasets include temperature and precipitation measurements, which help the system understand local climate patterns and seasonal variations. This information is particularly important because different crops have different temperature requirements and water needs. Combining satellite-based observations with soil sensor readings allows AgriOrbit to consider both underground soil conditions and external environmental factors.

Crop Rotation Recommendation

After collecting and analyzing the required data, AgriOrbit generates crop rotation recommendations for two consecutive growing seasons. The system considers the current nutrient status of the soil, its pH level, environmental conditions, and the characteristics of different crops.

An important factor in this process is the relationship between crops and soil nutrients. Continuous cultivation of the same crop can gradually increase the demand for specific nutrients, potentially contributing to soil depletion. However, rotating crops with different nutritional requirements can help distribute nutrient demands more effectively. For example, including suitable leguminous crops in a rotation plan can contribute to nitrogen management through biological nitrogen fixation.

The recommendation process also considers the farmer's preferences and available resources. Farmers can specify their preferred crops, available water quantity, and other relevant agricultural limitations. AgriOrbit uses these inputs alongside the collected environmental and soil data to identify suitable crop combinations and rotation sequences.

The system does not simply recommend crops based on their individual suitability. It evaluates how the first selected crop may influence soil conditions and how those conditions could affect the second growing season. This consecutive-season approach makes the recommendations more meaningful because it considers the long-term relationship between agricultural choices and soil health.

Expected Impact and Sustainability

AgriOrbit aims to support more sustainable agricultural practices by helping farmers reduce excessive nutrient depletion, use available water resources more efficiently, and select crops that are better suited to their local environmental conditions.

Furthermore, the integration of NASA Earth observation data demonstrates how space technology can contribute to solving practical challenges on Earth. Satellite observations provide valuable environmental information that, when combined with local soil measurements, can support agricultural planning at the field level.
